mainTopic: Dream signs, lists of three, and blessings on seeing places in בבל
overview: The amud opens with רבי יוחנן: a verse that comes to mind on waking is a small נבואה. The חכמים then list what it means to see certain kings, books of תנ"ך, and sages in a dream. Next come rules of the form “all are good in a dream except…” for animals, metals, fruit, vegetables, colors, and birds. Short challenges about the elephant and turnip heads are answered with small details. Memory aids then introduce groups of lists: things that do or do not benefit the body, tastes of עולם הבא (where תשמיש is explained as relieving oneself), things that one-sixtieth resemble something greater, and signs and foods that help or harm the sick. A ברייתא interprets dreams of a dead person in the house. The גמרא then turns to blessings: for מרקוליס, for a place cleared of עבודה זרה, and the five blessings of רב המנונא on seeing the ruins of בבל. It closes with stories of רבא and מר בריה דרבינא, and רב אשי's report that he said all five blessings on his own reasoning.

steps.title: A verse that comes to mind upon waking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן calls a verse that spontaneously comes to mind upon waking a small prophecy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says that if someone wakes and a verse comes into his mouth, this is a small prophecy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a meaning to a verse that comes to someone upon waking. This also sets up the following list of meaningful experiences around sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person does not choose a verse to say. The statement concerns one that comes to mind on its own.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If he woke early and a verse fell into his mouth—
this is a small prophecy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unprompted verse that comes to mind upon waking is called נְבוּאָה קְטַנָּה.

steps.title: Dream signs involving three kings
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים assign a different dream sign to each of three kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים teach: Seeing דָּוִד in a dream points to piety, שְׁלֹמֹה to wisdom, and אַחְאָב to possible trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים begin a list of dream signs with three kings. Each king has a different expected outcome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דָּוִד and שְׁלֹמֹה lead the dreamer to expect something good. אַחְאָב instead gives the dreamer reason for concern.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: There are three kings:
One who sees David in a dream should expect piety.
Solomon—he should expect wisdom.
Ahab—he should be concerned about calamity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a verse upon waking to a new list about dreams.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dreams of דָּוִד, שְׁלֹמֹה, and אַחְאָב carry different signs.

steps.title: Dream signs involving prophetic books and figures
steps.stepSummary: The list moves to מְלָכִים, יְחֶזְקֵאל, יְשַׁעְיָה, and יִרְמְיָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Seeing the book of מְלָכִים points to greatness; יְחֶזְקֵאל to wisdom; יְשַׁעְיָה to consolation; and יִרְמְיָה to concern about calamity.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים continue the dream list with prophetic writings. The outcomes now include greatness and consolation, as well as wisdom and concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each named sight receives its own sign. The wording mentions the book of מְלָכִים explicitly, then names three prophets without repeating “book of.”

keyTerms.meaning: prophets; also the Prophets section of the Bible

steps.confusionAlert: The heading says “three,” but the text gives four entries: מְלָכִים and three named prophets. Keep all four entries in the list.

phrases.english: There are three prophets:
One who sees the book of Kings should expect greatness.
Ezekiel—he should expect wisdom.
Isaiah—he should expect consolation.
Jeremiah—he should be concerned about calamity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the dream-sign list with a new group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The listed prophetic writings and figures signal greatness, wisdom, consolation, or concern about calamity.

steps.title: Dream signs involving three large books of כְּתוּבִים
steps.stepSummary: תְּהִלִּים, מִשְׁלֵי, and אִיּוֹב receive three different dream meanings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Seeing תְּהִלִּים points to piety, מִשְׁלֵי to wisdom, and אִיּוֹב to concern about calamity.
steps.whatsHappening: The list moves to three large books of כְּתוּבִים. It gives one sign for each book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This group returns to the same three outcomes used for the kings: piety, wisdom, and concern about calamity. Only the things seen in the dream have changed.

keyTerms.meaning: Writings, a section of the Bible

phrases.english: There are three large books of Writings:
One who sees the book of Psalms should expect piety,
Proverbs—he should expect wisdom,
Job—he should be concerned about calamity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the dream-sign list, now turning from נְבִיאִים to כְּתוּבִים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תְּהִלִּים signals piety, מִשְׁלֵי wisdom, and אִיּוֹב concern about calamity.

steps.title: Dream signs involving three small books of כְּתוּבִים
steps.stepSummary: שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים, קֹהֶלֶת, and קִינוֹת follow the same three-outcome pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: Seeing שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים in a dream points to piety, קֹהֶלֶת to wisdom, and קִינוֹת to concern about calamity.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give a second group of three books of כְּתוּבִים. The signs again follow the pattern of piety, wisdom, and concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heading changes from large books to small books. The meanings attached to the first, second, and third items remain in the same order.

phrases.english: There are three small books of Writings:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹאֶה שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים בַּחֲלוֹם — יְצַפֶּה לַחֲסִידוּת.
phrases.english: One who sees Song of Songs in a dream should expect piety.
Ecclesiastes—he should expect wisdom.
Lamentations—he should be concerned about calamity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second group of books from כְּתוּבִים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three named small books signal piety, wisdom, and concern about calamity, respectively.

steps.title: A distinct dream sign for מְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר
steps.stepSummary: Seeing מְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר signals that a miracle will happen for the dreamer.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sees מְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר: a miracle will be performed for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The list adds one more book after the group of three. This book receives its own sign: a miracle for the dreamer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous three books followed a repeated pattern. מְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר is stated separately and has a different outcome.
steps.whatToRemember: The dream lists often repeat a three-part pattern, but מְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר adds a separate sign: a miracle.

phrases.english: One who sees the Scroll of Esther—
a miracle is performed for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate dream sign after the three small books.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing מְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר signals that a miracle will be performed for the dreamer.

steps.title: Three sages as dream signs
steps.stepSummary: Seeing each of three חֲכָמִים has a different meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Seeing רַבִּי points to wisdom; seeing רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה points to wealth; seeing רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן אֱלִישָׁע calls for concern about calamity.
steps.whatsHappening: The list moves from books to people seen in dreams. It gives a separate sign for each of three sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same kind of dream—seeing a sage—does not always have the same meaning. The person seen determines the sign.

phrases.english: There are three sages:
One who sees Rabbi in a dream should expect wisdom.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה — יְצַפֶּה לַעֲשִׁירוּת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya—one should expect wealth.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן אֱלִישָׁע — יִדְאַג מִן הַפּוּרְעָנוּת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha—one should worry about calamity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier list of dream signs, now turning from books to sages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of these three sages signals a different outcome when seen in a dream.

steps.title: Three Torah scholars as dream signs
steps.stepSummary: A second group of three people also receives three different dream meanings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Seeing בֶּן עַזַּאי points to piety, בֶּן זוֹמָא to wisdom, and אַחֵר to concern about calamity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another three-person list. Again, the meaning depends on exactly whom the dreamer sees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This group follows the same pattern as the previous one: two favorable signs and one troubling sign. It is a new list, not a correction of the first.

phrases.english: There are three Torah scholars:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹאֶה בֶּן עַזַּאי בַּחֲלוֹם — יְצַפֶּה לַחֲסִידוּת.
phrases.english: One who sees Ben Azzai in a dream should expect piety.
Ben Zoma—one should expect wisdom.
Aḥer—one should worry about calamity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another three-person list using the same dream-sign format.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These three Torah scholars each indicate a distinct dream outcome.

steps.title: Animals are generally favorable dream signs
steps.stepSummary: Animals are called favorable dream signs, with three named exceptions.
steps.simpleTranslation: All kinds of animals are good to see in a dream, except an elephant, a monkey, and a long-tailed ape.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new kind of list: a general favorable rule followed by exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elephant is explicitly placed among the exceptions. That detail sets up the question that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: a long-tailed ape in this context

phrases.english: All kinds of animals are favorable in a dream,
except for the elephant, the monkey, and the long-tailed ape.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from named people to categories of things seen in dreams.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals are generally favorable dream signs, apart from three specified animals.

steps.title: An elephant can also signal a miracle
steps.stepSummary: An earlier statement seems to give the elephant a favorable meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn’t the Master say that someone who sees an elephant in a dream will have a miracle happen for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the elephant exception. It quotes a statement that treats seeing an elephant as a good sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 called an elephant an exception to favorable animal dreams. This statement says an elephant can signal a miracle, so the two descriptions need to be reconciled.

phrases.english: But didn’t the Master say: One who sees an elephant in a dream
will have a miracle happen for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the listed elephant exception.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an elephant is an unfavorable exception.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A separate statement says seeing an elephant signals a miracle.

steps.title: The elephant’s equipment changes the sign
steps.stepSummary: The two statements describe elephants seen in different ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no difficulty: the favorable sign concerns a saddled elephant; the exception concerns one that is not saddled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by distinguishing between two versions of the dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements can stand. Seeing the elephant saddled signals a miracle; seeing it without a saddle remains the exception.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
this is when it is saddled,
and this is when it is not saddled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent conflict by adding a detail about the elephant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases by whether the elephant is saddled.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two statements appeared to discuss the same sight of an elephant.
steps.terutzMaskana: A saddled elephant is favorable; an unsaddled elephant is the exception.

steps.title: Metal objects and the importance of handles
steps.stepSummary: Metal objects are generally favorable, with three exceptions when seen on their handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: All kinds of metal objects are good dream signs, except a hoe, chisel, and axe. The exception applies when those tools are seen on their handles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to metal objects. It immediately specifies what the three exceptional tools look like in the dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The qualification limits the exception; it does not change the general statement about metal objects. The tools’ handles are part of the dream image being discussed.

phrases.english: All kinds of metal objects are favorable in a dream,
except for a hoe, a chisel, and an axe.
And this applies when one sees them on their handles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins another general-rule-and-exceptions list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Metal objects are generally favorable dream signs; three handled tools are exceptions.

steps.title: Fruit is favorable except for unripe dates
steps.stepSummary: The fruit list gives one exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: All kinds of fruit are favorable dream signs, except unripe dates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short new rule about fruit seen in dreams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern stays the same: a broad favorable category followed by a specific exception.

phrases.english: All kinds of fruit are favorable in a dream,
except for unripe dates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the sequence of dream-sign categories, now with fruit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit is generally favorable in dreams, except for unripe dates.

steps.title: Vegetables are favorable except for turnip heads
steps.stepSummary: The vegetable list names turnip heads as its exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: All kinds of vegetables are favorable dream signs, except turnip heads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the rule for vegetables. Its exception sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turnip heads are singled out as unfavorable here. The next statement will describe someone who saw them before becoming wealthy.

phrases.english: All kinds of vegetables are favorable in a dream,
except for turnip heads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from fruit to vegetables while keeping the same rule-and-exception format.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vegetables are generally favorable dream signs, apart from turnip heads.

steps.title: רב saw turnip heads before becoming wealthy
steps.stepSummary: רַב’s experience seems to challenge the vegetable exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn’t רַב say, ‘I did not become wealthy until I saw turnip heads’?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim about turnip heads by quoting רַב’s own experience.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If seeing turnip heads preceded רַב’s wealth, they seem to be a favorable sign. That appears to conflict with step 14.

phrases.english: But didn’t Rav say: I did not become wealthy
until I saw turnip heads!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the newly stated turnip-head exception.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that turnip heads are an exception to favorable vegetable dreams.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רַב connects seeing turnip heads with his later wealth.

steps.title: רב saw the turnip heads on their stems
steps.stepSummary: A detail of what רַב saw distinguishes his dream from the exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he saw them, he saw them on their stems.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adding a detail to רַב’s dream: the turnip heads were on their stems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that רַב saw turnip heads in the same form meant by the exception. The answer says his dream was different, so his favorable experience does not overturn that exception.

phrases.english: When he saw them—
he saw them on their stems.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by specifying how the turnips appeared.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by whether the turnip heads were seen on their stems.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רַב’s dream seemed to match the unfavorable turnip-head exception.
steps.terutzMaskana: רַב saw turnip heads on their stems, a different dream image.

steps.title: Colors are favorable except for sky-blue
steps.stepSummary: The color list has one named exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: All kinds of colors are favorable in a dream, except sky-blue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to colors and states another general rule with an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new category of dream signs. The text names the exception but does not explain it here.

phrases.english: All kinds of colors are favorable in a dream,
except for sky-blue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to listing dream-sign categories after the turnip-head exchange.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Colors are generally favorable dream signs, except for sky-blue.

steps.title: Birds are favorable with three exceptions
steps.stepSummary: The final list here names three birds as exceptions.
steps.simpleTranslation: All kinds of birds are favorable in a dream, except קַרְיָא, קִפּוֹפָא, and קוּרְפְּרַאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more general dream rule, this time about birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As with the other lists, the rule is favorable unless the dream contains one of the named exceptions. No question or answer follows next.

keyTerms.meaning: a bird named as an exception
a bird named as an exception

phrases.english: All kinds of birds are favorable in a dream,
except for the karia, the kipofa, and the kurperai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds birds after the list of colors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds are generally favorable dream signs, apart from three named exceptions.
steps.whatToRemember: In these lists, first find the general rule, then its exceptions. In the two challenges, a small detail—an elephant’s saddle or turnips on their stems—explains why both statements can stand.

steps.title: A memory aid introduces five lists
steps.stepSummary: The opening words point to the five lists that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The body, the body, a taste of, restore, and broaden: a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next five lists with a memory aid. Each word points to a list that is about to appear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two mentions of “the body” point to two different lists. This line does not give the lists themselves; it helps the learner keep track of their order.

keyTerms.meaning: something resembling or giving a taste of

phrases.english: (The body, the body, a taste of,
restore, and broaden: a memory aid).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier list of birds, this line prepares a new set of lists.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory aid gives the order of the five lists.

steps.title: Three foods enter the body without benefiting it
steps.stepSummary: The first list names three foods that enter the body but do not help it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three things enter the body, yet the body does not benefit from them: cherries, poor-quality dates, and unripe dates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first list promised by the memory aid. It names foods that are eaten but do not benefit the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: “Enter the body” refers to eating them. The point of this list is the contrast between entering the body and benefiting it.

phrases.english: Three things enter the body,
yet the body does not benefit from them:
cherries, poor-quality dates, and unripe dates.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה נִכְנָסִין לַגּוּף, וְאֵין הַגּוּף נֶהֱנֶה מֵהֶן:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first “body” list announced by the memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These three foods enter the body but do not benefit it.

steps.title: Three things benefit the body without entering it
steps.stepSummary: The second list reverses the pattern of the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three things do not enter the body, yet the body benefits from them. They are washing, anointing, and usage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second body list. This time, the beneficial things do not enter the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contrast with the previous list is deliberate: something can help the body without being eaten. Here תַּשְׁמִישׁ is listed without further explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: usage; a word whose meaning depends on context

phrases.english: Three things do not enter the body,
yet the body benefits from them; they are:
washing, anointing, and usage.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵין נִכְנָסִין לַגּוּף, וְהַגּוּף נֶהֱנֶה מֵהֶן, אֵלּוּ הֵן:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It reverses the first list’s contrast between entering and benefiting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These three things benefit the body without entering it.

steps.title: Three experiences offer a taste of עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: The third list names שַׁבָּת, the sun, and תַּשְׁמִישׁ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three things are a taste of עולם הבא. They are שבת, the sun, and usage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third list. It names three experiences that offer a taste of עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תַּשְׁמִישׁ appears again, but the list gives no explanation of what kind of usage it means. That uncertainty leads to the next question.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, אֵלּוּ הֵן:
phrases.english: Three things are a taste of the World-to-Come; they are:
the Sabbath, the sun, and usage.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, אֵלּוּ הֵן:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The memory aid now moves from the two body lists to its third list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שַׁבָּת, the sun, and תַּשְׁמִישׁ are described as a taste of עוֹלָם הַבָּא.

steps.title: Which kind of usage does the list mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what תַּשְׁמִישׁ means in the second and third lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: Usage of what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of תַּשְׁמִישׁ in the two lists that mention it: things that benefit the body and things that give a taste of עוֹלָם הַבָּא. It is setting up a possible interpretation to test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תַּשְׁמִישׁ is a broad word. The question is which activity fits these lists.

phrases.english: Usage of what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks about the final item in the list just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which meaning of תַּשְׁמִישׁ fits the lists about benefiting the body and about עוֹלָם הַבָּא?

steps.title: Conjugal relations do not seem to fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests one meaning of תַּשְׁמִישׁ and objects that it weakens the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means conjugal relations—does that not weaken a person?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries reading תַּשְׁמִישׁ as conjugal relations, then challenges that reading. It says this activity weakens a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that weakens the body cannot be listed as benefiting the body, nor as a taste of עוֹלָם הַבָּא. The challenge is about how to understand the word, not about removing it from the lists.

keyTerms.meaning: the bed; here, part of an expression for conjugal relations

phrases.english: If you say it means conjugal relations—
does that not weaken a person!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא תַּשְׁמִישׁ הַמִּטָּה — הָא מִכְחָשׁ כָּחֵישׁ!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It tests a possible answer to the question and raises a problem with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading תַּשְׁמִישׁ in the lists about benefiting the body and about עוֹלָם הַבָּא as תַּשְׁמִישׁ הַמִּטָּה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תַּשְׁמִישׁ הַמִּטָּה weakens the body. It cannot be something the body benefits from, nor a taste of עוֹלָם הַבָּא.

steps.title: The intended usage is relieving oneself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supplies a different meaning of תַּשְׁמִישׁ for this list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means using one’s bodily openings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that תַּשְׁמִישׁ here means relieving oneself. This replaces the meaning challenged in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer keeps תַּשְׁמִישׁ in the list but identifies a different activity. The issue was the meaning of the word in this context, not whether the listed item should be removed.
steps.whatToRemember: In both lists (benefiting the body and a taste of עוֹלָם הַבָּא), תַּשְׁמִישׁ is explained as relieving oneself.

phrases.english: Rather, using one’s bodily openings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It resolves the challenge by giving תַּשְׁמִישׁ a different meaning here.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies which meaning of an ambiguous word fits this list.

steps.title: Three things restore a person’s state of mind
steps.stepSummary: The fourth list names voice, sight, and smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three things restore a person’s state of mind. They are voice, sight, and smell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the lists announced by the memory aid. It names three things that restore a person’s state of mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of תַּשְׁמִישׁ is finished. This is a new list, centered on what a person hears, sees, and smells.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה מְשִׁיבִין דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם, אֵלּוּ הֵן:
phrases.english: Three things restore a person’s state of mind; they are:
voice, sight, and smell.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה מְשִׁיבִין דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם, אֵלּוּ הֵן:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After clarifying תַּשְׁמִישׁ, the גמרא resumes the sequence of lists.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Voice, sight, and smell restore a person’s state of mind.

steps.title: Three things broaden a person’s state of mind
steps.stepSummary: The final list names a pleasant home, wife, and belongings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three things broaden a person’s state of mind. They are a beautiful dwelling, a beautiful wife, and beautiful vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the fifth and final list announced by the memory aid. It names three pleasant parts of a person’s surroundings and life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous list described voice, sight, and smell. This list shifts to a dwelling, a wife, and belongings as things that broaden a person’s state of mind.

keyTerms.meaning: broaden or give a sense of ease

steps.whatToRemember: The memory aid’s five lists are now complete: two about the body, one about עוֹלָם הַבָּא, one about restoring a person’s state of mind, and one about broadening it.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה מַרְחִיבִין דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם, אֵלּוּ הֵן:
phrases.english: Three things broaden a person’s state of mind; they are:

phrases.aramaic: דִּירָה נָאָה, וְאִשָּׁה נָאָה, וְכֵלִים נָאִים.
phrases.english: a beautiful dwelling, a beautiful wife, and beautiful vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה מַרְחִיבִין דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם, אֵלּוּ הֵן:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It supplies the last list in the memory aid’s sequence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A beautiful dwelling, wife, and belongings broaden a person’s state of mind.

steps.title: A memory aid for the next lists
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the numbers five, six, and ten as a סימן to remember the lists that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five, six, and ten: this is a memory sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It gives a short memory code, 'five, six, ten,' so we can remember the lists that are coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line teaches no law or idea by itself. It is a table of contents in number form: a list of five, a list of six, and a list of ten. That helps the learner keep track of the order.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign or mnemonic. Here it is a code to remember the lists. In the next lists the same word means 'omen'.

steps.confusionAlert: The word סִימָן has two meanings in this passage. Here it means a memory aid. In the 'six things' list (step 30) it means a good omen for a sick person.

phrases.english: Five, six, and ten are a memory sign:
phrases.notes: A list of five, then six, then ten will follow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of numbered lists and introduces the next group of lists.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory code (5, 6, 10) for the coming lists.

steps.title: Five things that are one-sixtieth of something greater
steps.stepSummary: Fire, honey, שבת, sleep, and a dream are each a small taste (one-sixtieth) of a bigger version: גיהנם, מן, עולם הבא, death, and נבואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five things are one-sixtieth: fire, honey, שבת, sleep, and a dream. Fire is one-sixtieth of גיהנם. Honey is one-sixtieth of the מן. שבת is one-sixtieth of עולם הבא. Sleep is one-sixtieth of death. A dream is one-sixtieth of נבואה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first list, the 'five.' It names five things we know in this world and says each one is a small sample of a much bigger thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the list is named. Then each item is paired with its 'full version.' The idea is that ordinary experiences give us a tiny taste of spiritual realities. For example, the rest of שבת gives a taste of עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: One-sixtieth: a small portion or taste of something bigger
גיהנם, the place of punishment after death
The מן (manna) eaten in the desert

phrases.english: Five things are one-sixtieth,
and these are they: fire, honey, and Shabbat,
and sleep, and a dream.
Fire is one-sixtieth of Gehenna.
Honey is one-sixtieth of the manna.
Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the World to Come.
Sleep is one-sixtieth of death.
A dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy.
phrases.notes: This connects to the larger topic of dreams in this part of the מסכת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the 'five' from the memory sign.
steps.whyThisMatters: The pairing of a dream with נבואה ties this list to the larger discussion of dreams on this דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fire, honey, שבת, sleep, and dreams are each a one-sixtieth taste of גיהנם, מן, עולם הבא, death, and נבואה.

steps.title: Six good signs for a sick person
steps.stepSummary: Sneezing, sweating, loose bowels, a seminal emission, sleep, and a dream are good signs for someone who is ill.
steps.simpleTranslation: Six things are a good sign for a sick person: sneezing, sweating, loose bowels, a seminal emission, sleep, and a dream.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the 'six' list. It names six bodily signs that show a sick person is getting better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here סימן means an omen, not a memory aid. These are normal body functions. When they return in a sick person, it shows the body is healing. The next step brings a פסוק for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: A good sign or good omen

phrases.english: Six things are a good sign for a sick person,
and these are they: sneezing, sweating, loose bowels,
a seminal emission, sleep, and a dream.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'five' list to the first 'six' list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six bodily signs are good omens for a sick person.

steps.title: A verse for each good sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק to support each of the six good signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sneezing, as it says: 'His sneezes flash forth light.' Sweat, as it says: 'By the sweat of your face you will eat bread.' Loose bowels, as it says: 'The one bent down will quickly be released, and he will not die into the pit.' A seminal emission, as it says: 'He will see children and live long.' Sleep, as it says: 'I would have slept; then I would be at rest.' A dream, as it says: 'You heal me (וְתַחֲלִימֵנִי) and give me life.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the six signs one at a time. For each one it shows a פסוק that links it to light, life, or healing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק connects the sign to good health. Sneezing brings 'light,' sweat goes with eating bread (living), loose bowels means being 'released' and not dying, an emission links to 'seed' and long life, and sleep brings 'rest.' For dreams, the word וְתַחֲלִימֵנִי sounds like חֲלוֹם, a dream.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written; introduces a פסוק as a source
'And You heal me.' It is read as related to חֲלוֹם (dream).
The pit, meaning death or the grave

phrases.english: Sneezing, as it is written: "His sneezes flash forth light" (Job 41:10).
phrases.notes: A sneeze is a sign the person will see the light of life.

phrases.english: Sweat, as it is written: "By the sweat of your face shall you eat bread" (Genesis 3:19).
Loose bowels, as it is written:
"He who is bent down shall quickly be loosed, and he shall not die into the pit" (Isaiah 51:14).
A seminal emission, as it is written: "He shall see seed, he shall prolong days" (Isaiah 53:10).
Sleep, as it is written: "I would have slept; then I would have rest" (Job 3:13).
A dream, as it is written: "And You heal me and make me live" (Isaiah 38:16).
phrases.notes: וְתַחֲלִימֵנִי is read as related to חֲלוֹם, a dream.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports each item of the six-sign list with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That each of the six signs is a good omen for a sick person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: פסוקים from איוב, בראשית, and ישעיה that link each sign to light, life, rest, or healing.

steps.title: Six foods that heal a sick person
steps.stepSummary: Cabbage, beets, dried סיסין, stomach, placenta, and the lobe of the liver truly heal a sick person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Six things heal a sick person from his illness, and the healing is a real healing: cabbage, beets, dried סיסין, the stomach, the placenta, and the lobe of the liver.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second 'six' list: six foods that cure a sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words וּרְפוּאָתוֹ רְפוּאָה add that the cure is real and lasting, not a short-term relief. The list has plant foods (cabbage, beets, סיסין) and animal parts (stomach, placenta, liver lobe).

keyTerms.meaning: And its cure is a real cure, an effective healing
The lobe of the liver (Sefaria: diaphragm)

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים מְרַפְּאִין אֶת הַחוֹלֶה מֵחׇלְיוֹ
phrases.english: Six things heal a sick person from his illness
and its cure is a real cure,

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ הֵן: כְּרוּב, וּתְרָדִין, וְסִיסִין יְבֵשִׁין,
phrases.english: and these are they: cabbage, beets, dried foley,
the stomach, the placenta, and the lobe of the liver.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים מְרַפְּאִין אֶת הַחוֹלֶה מֵחׇלְיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from signs of healing to things that cause healing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six foods give a sick person a true cure.

steps.title: Some add small fish, which strengthen the whole body
steps.stepSummary: A יש אומרים adds small fish to the healing list and says they make the whole body thrive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: small fish also heal. And more than that: small fish make a person's whole body fruitful and healthy.
steps.whatsHappening: An extra opinion, יש אומרים, adds a seventh item to the healing list: small fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יש אומרים does more than add fish to the list. With וְלָא עוֹד אֶלָּא it says small fish do even more than the other foods: they strengthen the whole body, not just cure the illness.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only that, but even more

phrases.english: And some say: small fish as well.
And not only that, but small fish

phrases.aramaic: מַפְרִין וּמַבְרִין כׇּל גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם.
phrases.english: make a person's entire body flourish and become healthy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the healing list with an added opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to יש אומרים, small fish also heal and strengthen the entire body.

steps.title: Ten things that bring an illness back
steps.stepSummary: Ten foods and activities can make a recovering person relapse, and the illness comes back worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ten things bring a sick person back to his illness, and the illness is severe: eating beef, fatty meat, roasted meat, poultry, a roasted egg, shaving, cress, milk, cheese, and the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the 'ten' list, the last number in the memory sign. These are things a recovering person should avoid because they can bring the sickness back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list is the opposite of the healing list. The words וְחׇלְיוֹ קָשֶׁה add that the relapse is worse than the first illness. Most items are heavy foods, but shaving and the bathhouse are activities, not foods.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring him back to his illness (cause a relapse)

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים מַחֲזִירִין אֶת הַחוֹלֶה לְחׇלְיוֹ,
phrases.english: Ten things bring a sick person back to his illness,
and his illness is severe, and these are they:
one who eats ox meat, fatty meat,
roasted meat, poultry,
a roasted egg, shaving, cress,
milk, cheese, and the bathhouse.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים מַחֲזִירִין אֶת הַחוֹלֶה לְחׇלְיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the healing list by listing things that cause relapse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten things cause a recovering person to relapse more severely.

steps.title: Some add nuts and cucumbers to the relapse list
steps.stepSummary: Two more opinions add nuts and cucumbers to the list of things that bring illness back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: nuts too. And some say: cucumbers too.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more opinions each add one item to the relapse list: nuts, and cucumbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The core list stays at ten, matching the memory sign. The יש אומרים opinions extend it with more foods that can harm a recovering person, just as small fish were added to the healing list.
steps.whatToRemember: This passage finishes the 'five, six, ten' memory sign: five things that are a one-sixtieth taste of something greater, six good signs for the sick (each with a פסוק), six foods that heal (plus small fish), and ten things that cause relapse (plus nuts and cucumbers).

phrases.english: And some say: nuts as well.
And some say: cucumbers as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds opinions that extend the relapse list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some add nuts, and some add cucumbers, to the things that cause relapse.

steps.title: Why cucumbers have their name
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל says cucumbers are harmful to the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are cucumbers called קישואים? Because they are as hard on the body as swords.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a wordplay to explain the warning about cucumbers mentioned earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching links the sound of קישואים to קשים, meaning harmful. It presents the harm as a general statement, which the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
Why are they called cucumbers?
Because they are as harmful to the body as swords.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the warning about cucumbers added in step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cucumbers are described as harmful to the body.

steps.title: Why did the wealthy keep serving cucumbers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the warning by citing a teaching that cucumbers were always on the tables of אנטונינוס and רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? Scripture says, “Two nations are in your womb.” Read “nations” as “proud ones.” רב יהודה said in the name of רב that these are אנטונינוס and רבי, whose tables never lacked radish, lettuce, or cucumbers, in summer or in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how cucumbers can be so harmful if two prominent people served them throughout the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is read as referring to אנטונינוס and רבי, and their tables are described as exceptionally well supplied. Cucumbers on those tables appear to clash with the earlier warning.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as written.
The prominent figure named alongside רבי.

phrases.english: Is that so? But is it not written:
“And the Lord said to her: Two nations are in your womb”:
Do not read “nations,” but “proud ones,”
and Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
These are Antoninus and Rabbi,
whose tables never lacked

phrases.aramaic: לֹא צְנוֹן וְלֹא חֲזֶרֶת וְלֹא קִשּׁוּאִין,
phrases.english: radish, lettuce, or cucumbers,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וְלֹא בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים.
phrases.english: neither in summer nor in the rainy season.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the broad warning about cucumbers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 36 that cucumbers harm the body.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cucumbers were consistently served at the distinguished tables of אנטונינוס and רבי.

steps.title: Cucumber size resolves the conflict
steps.stepSummary: The harmful cucumbers are large ones; the cucumbers served on those tables are small ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no difficulty: this refers to large ones, and that refers to small ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the apparent contradiction by distinguishing between cucumber sizes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning applies to large cucumbers. The account of the well-supplied tables applies to small cucumbers, so the two statements can both stand.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this refers to large ones,
and that refers to small ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּרַבְרְבֵי, הָא בְּזוּטְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting each statement to a different size.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements concern cucumbers of the same size.
steps.terutzMaskana: Large cucumbers are the harmful ones; small cucumbers are the ones served on the tables.

steps.title: Dream signs involving a dead person at home
steps.stepSummary: A teaching lists three signs in a dream: a dead person in the house, eating or drinking there, and taking items away.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: A dead person in the house means peace in the house. If the dead person ate and drank there, it is a good sign for the house. If the dead person took items from it, it is a bad sign for the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new list of dream signs involving a dead person in a house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply seeing the dead person, or seeing them eat and drink, is read positively. The list initially describes taking items from the house as a bad sign; the next step narrows that statement.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead person in the house.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A dead person in the house—peace in the house.
If the dead person ate and drank in the house—
it is a good sign for the house.
If the dead person took items from the house—
it is a bad sign for the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a separate set of dream interpretations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dream teaching assigns different signs to what the dead person does in the house.

steps.title: The bad sign concerns footwear
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits the bad sign about taking items to shoes and sandals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא explained it as referring to a shoe and a sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא narrows the previous teaching’s statement about items taken from the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bad sign does not apply to every item a dead person takes in a dream. It refers specifically to footwear, as the next rule makes clear.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it as referring to a particular case.
The Sage who explains the previous teaching.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa explained it
as referring to a shoe and a sandal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the previous step’s bad sign to particular items.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any item taken by the dead person is a bad sign.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bad sign concerns a shoe or sandal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא limits the bad sign of a dead person taking items to a shoe and a sandal.

steps.title: What a dead person takes in a dream
steps.stepSummary: The general rule treats items taken by a dead person as a good sign, apart from footwear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything a dead person takes is a good sign, except a shoe and a sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the broader rule that supports רב פפא’s narrow reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking an item is normally a good sign in this dream teaching. Footwear is the stated exception, so it explains why the earlier bad sign needed a limit.

phrases.english: Anything a dead person takes is a good sign,
except a shoe and a sandal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the general rule behind רב פפא’s explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: What the dead person takes is generally a good sign, except footwear.

steps.title: What a dead person gives in a dream
steps.stepSummary: Items given by a dead person are generally a good sign, except dust and mustard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything a dead person gives is a good sign, except dust and mustard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a parallel rule for a dream in which the dead person gives something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The direction changes from taking to giving, but the general sign remains positive. This rule names two different exceptions: dust and mustard.

phrases.english: Anything a dead person gives is a good sign,
except dust and mustard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the matching rule for items given rather than taken.
steps.whatToRemember: In these dream rules, taking and giving are usually good signs, but each has its own named exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: What the dead person gives is generally a good sign, except dust and mustard.

steps.title: A blessing on seeing מרקוליס
steps.stepSummary: A reference to a place cleared of עבודה זרה sets up a new topic; the teaching first gives a blessing for seeing מרקוליס.
steps.simpleTranslation: A place from which עבודה זרה was removed. The חכמים taught: One who sees מרקוליס says, “Blessed … who has shown patience to those who violate His will.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from dreams to blessings connected with עבודה זרה. The opening words recall the case of a place where it was removed, setting up the new teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before discussing that place, the teaching gives a different case: seeing מרקוליס itself. Its blessing speaks of God’s patience toward people acting against His will.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who act against His will.

phrases.english: A place from which idolatry was removed.
The Sages taught:
One who sees Mercury says:
“Blessed … who has shown patience
to those who violate His will.”

steps.triggerLanguage: מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּעֶקְרָה מִמֶּנּוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹאֶה מַרְקוּלִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the dream discussion and opens the topic of blessings concerning עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing מרקוליס calls for a blessing about God’s patience.

steps.title: A blessing where עבודה זרה was removed
steps.stepSummary: The teaching gives the blessing and added request for a place where עבודה זרה was uprooted.
steps.simpleTranslation: At a place from which עבודה זרה was removed, one says: “Blessed … who uprooted עבודה זרה from our land. Just as it was uprooted from this place, may it be uprooted from all places of ישראל, and turn the hearts of its worshippers to serve You.”
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching now addresses the place mentioned in its opening line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing thanks God for what happened at this place. It then asks for עבודה זרה to be removed elsewhere and for its worshippers’ hearts to turn toward serving God.

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּעֶקְרָה מִמֶּנּוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: At a place from which idolatry was removed, one says:
“Blessed … who uprooted idolatry from our land.
And just as it was uprooted from this place,
so may it be uprooted from all places of Israel,
and turn the hearts of its worshippers to serve You.”

steps.triggerLanguage: מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּעֶקְרָה מִמֶּנּוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the place named at the start of the new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blessing for a place cleared of עבודה זרה includes thanks and a request for further removal and changed hearts.

steps.title: A shorter wording outside the land
steps.stepSummary: The teaching says that outside the land, one need not say the request to turn the worshippers’ hearts.
steps.simpleTranslation: In חוץ לארץ, one need not say, “And turn the hearts of its worshippers to serve You,” because most of its people are גויים.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching limits one part of the previous blessing when it is said outside the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stated reason is that most people there are גויים. The text removes only the quoted request about the worshippers’ hearts; it does not say to omit the whole blessing.

phrases.english: And outside the land one need not say
“And turn the hearts of its worshippers to serve You,”
because most of its people are gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the wording of the blessing given in step 44.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside the land, the request to turn the worshippers’ hearts need not be said.

steps.title: The request is said outside the land too
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees and supports including the request outside the land with a verse about the peoples.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Even in חוץ לארץ one must say it, because they are destined to convert, as it says: “Then I will turn the peoples to a pure language.”
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives a different ruling about the disputed words and cites a verse to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says to include the request even outside the land. His reason looks beyond the current population: the verse speaks of a future change among the peoples.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sage who disagrees with the preceding ruling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר כֵּן,
phrases.english: Even outside the land one must say it,
because they are destined to convert,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אָז אֶהְפֹּךְ אֶל עַמִּים שָׂפָה בְרוּרָה״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: “Then I will turn the peoples to a pure language.”

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the preceding opinion, which said the request need not be said outside the land.
steps.whatToRemember: The disagreement is about one request within the blessing outside the land, not about whether to say the blessing at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires the request about the worshippers’ hearts even outside the land.

steps.title: The five blessings begin with seeing בבל
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא introduces five blessings and gives the first, for seeing בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא taught that one who sees wicked בבל must recite five blessings. On seeing בבל, one says a blessing over its destruction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a list of five blessings associated with sights in בבל. It gives the first blessing now; the other four follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening count tells us to expect five blessings, not five separate visits. The first sight is בבל itself.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב הַמְנוּנָא: הָרוֹאֶה בָּבֶל הָרְשָׁעָה
phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna taught: One who sees wicked Babylonia
must recite five blessings.
If one saw Babylonia, one says:
“Blessed … Who destroyed wicked Babylonia.”
phrases.notes: The ellipsis appears in the source text.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב הַמְנוּנָא: הָרוֹאֶה בָּבֶל הָרְשָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of blessings connected to עבודה זרה, the גמרא opens a list of blessings for sights in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing specified sights in בבל calls for five blessings; the first concerns בבל itself.

steps.title: Seeing the house of נבוכדנצר
steps.stepSummary: The second blessing is for seeing the ruined house of נבוכדנצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one sees the house of נבוכדנצר, one blesses the One who destroyed the house of the wicked נבוכדנצר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second sight and its blessing. This one focuses on the house of נבוכדנצר rather than בבל as a whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first blessing named the destruction of בבל. This blessing names the destruction of a particular ruler’s house.

phrases.english: If one saw Nebuchadnezzar’s house, one says:
“Blessed … Who destroyed the house
of the wicked Nebuchadnezzar.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second blessing to רב המנונא’s list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing the house of נבוכדנצר calls for a blessing over its destruction.

steps.title: Seeing a place where a miracle occurred
steps.stepSummary: The third blessing is for the lions’ den or the fiery furnace.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one sees the lions’ den or the fiery furnace, one blesses the One who performed miracles for our ancestors at this place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third blessing, this time for a place associated with rescue. Either of the two named places prompts the same blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two blessings concerned destruction. This one instead thanks God for miracles at a particular location.

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה גּוֹב שֶׁל אֲרָיוֹת אוֹ כִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ, אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: If one saw a lions’ den or the fiery furnace, one says:
“Blessed … Who performed miracles for our ancestors
at this place.”

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה גּוֹב שֶׁל אֲרָיוֹת אוֹ כִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a miracle-site blessing after two blessings about destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing either named miracle site calls for the blessing for miracles performed there.

steps.title: Seeing מרקוליס
steps.stepSummary: The fourth blessing concerns God’s patience toward those who disobey Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one sees מרקוליס, one blesses the One who shows patience to those who violate His will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the blessing for seeing מרקוליס as the fourth item in this list. It then moves to a fifth, different sight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This blessing was already given in the preceding discussion. Here it appears again because רב המנונא counts it among the five blessings associated with these sights.

keyTerms.meaning: Merculis, an object of idolatrous worship
toward those who violate His will

phrases.english: If one saw Mercury, one says:
“Blessed … Who has shown patience
to those who violate His will.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the fourth item, explicitly repeating a blessing from the earlier עבודה זרה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing מרקוליס calls for a blessing about God’s patience toward those who violate His will.

steps.title: Seeing earth removed from בבל
steps.stepSummary: The fifth blessing marks the removal of earth as fulfillment of God’s decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one sees a place from which earth is taken, one blesses the One who speaks and acts, decrees and fulfills.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the list with a blessing for a place where earth is being removed. The next accounts will show how sages responded to that removal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing connects a visible action—the taking of earth—with a divine decree being carried out. This prepares the stories about people and animals moving בבל’s earth.

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה מָקוֹם שֶׁנּוֹטְלִין מִמֶּנּוּ עָפָר, אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: If one saw a place from which earth is taken, one says:
“Blessed … Who speaks and acts,
decrees and fulfills.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב המנונא’s five-blessing list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing a place from which בבל’s earth is removed calls for a blessing about God’s decree being fulfilled.

steps.title: רבא urges on the donkeys
steps.stepSummary: רבא treats donkeys carrying away בבל’s earth as participants in fulfilling God’s will.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבא saw donkeys carrying earth, he would slap their backs with his hand and say, “Run, righteous ones, to do your Master’s will.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an example of a sage reacting to earth being taken from בבל. רבא encourages the donkeys carrying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals are doing ordinary transport work, but רבא sees their work as helping bring about the removal of בבל’s earth. His words explain why he calls them “righteous.”

phrases.english: When Rava would see donkeys

phrases.aramaic: דְּשָׁקְלִי עַפְרָא, טָרֵיף לְהוּ יְדָא עַל גַּבַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: carrying earth, he would slap their backs with his hand,
and say: Run, righteous ones,
to do the will of your Master.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא כִּי הֲוָה חָזֵי חֲמָרֵי דְּשָׁקְלִי עַפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the significance of removing earth from בבל.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבינא removes earth himself
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא throws earth out of בבל to act on the verse about its destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: When מר בריה דרבינא reached בבל, he would put earth in his cloth and throw it outside, to fulfill the verse, “I will sweep it with the broom of destruction.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second example involving בבל’s earth. This time a sage removes some himself and connects his action to a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא encouraged animals that were already carrying earth away. מר בריה דרבינא personally takes earth out, making the verse’s image of sweeping especially vivid.

phrases.aramaic: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא כִּי הֲוָה מָטֵי לְבָבֶל
phrases.english: When Mar, son of Ravina, would reach Babylonia,
he would take earth in his cloth
and throw it outside, to fulfill what is written:
“And I will sweep it with the broom of destruction.”

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא כִּי הֲוָה מָטֵי לְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a personal action and a verse to the account of earth being removed from בבל.

steps.title: רב אשי reached the blessings independently
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says he had not heard רב המנונא’s teaching but recited all the blessings on his own reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: “I had not heard this teaching of רב המנונא. Rather, I recited all of these blessings based on my own reasoning.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this passage with רב אשי’s report. He says he recited the blessings even without having heard רב המנונא’s statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי is not challenging the list. He confirms that he said all its blessings, while explaining that he reached them independently.
steps.whatToRemember: רב המנונא gives five blessings; רב אשי says he recited all five without having heard that teaching.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: As for me,

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי,
phrases.english: I had not heard this teaching of Rav Hamnuna,
but I recited blessings for all of them based on my own reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲנָא, הָא דְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the examples to the full five-blessing teaching and closes the passage.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי reports reciting all five blessings independently of hearing רב המנונא’s teaching.
